items.text: The plan turned out to be financially {unviable|non-viable|nonviable}. (VIABLE)
There has been a {noticeable} improvement in sales. (NOTICE)
The {reliability} of the data has been questioned. (RELY)
Her {refusal} to compromise ended the talks. (REFUSE)
The changes were introduced with {remarkably} little resistance. (REMARK)
Most staff were {unaware} of the new policy. (AWARE)
We need to {strengthen} our position in the market. (STRONG)
The {likelihood} of a strike is now very low. (LIKE)
The report was criticised for its many {inaccuracies}. (ACCURATE)
items.hint: Negative prefix + noun, and it's plural.

items.text: The two offers are virtually {indistinguishable}. (DISTINGUISH)
To call the results 'disappointing' was an {understatement}. (STATE)
The company has a policy of complete {transparency} with investors. (TRANSPARENT)
Their {reluctance} to invest is understandable. (RELUCTANT)
The new design is a significant {departure} from the old one. (DEPART)
The {feasibility} of the project is still being assessed. (FEASIBLE)
Prices fluctuate {unpredictably} from month to month. (PREDICT)
She showed great {resilience} during the crisis. (RESILIENT)
The merger led to the {relocation} of our head office. (LOCATE)
His comments were {misleading}, to say the least. (LEAD)
We are {increasingly} dependent on a single supplier. (INCREASE)
The {proliferation} of cheap imports worries local firms. (PROLIFERATE)
Once signed, the agreement is legally {binding}. (BIND)
It would be {inadvisable} to sign without legal advice. (ADVISE)
The {acquisition} of the rival firm was completed in May. (ACQUIRE)
Customer {loyalty} is hard to win back. (LOYAL)
The outcome was entirely {foreseeable}. (FORESEE)
We need to {prioritise|prioritize} the key accounts. (PRIORITY)
The {disappearance} of small shops is a national trend. (APPEAR)
There has been widespread {dissatisfaction} with the new rota. (SATISFY)
viable → noun: {viability} · opposite: {unviable|non-viable|nonviable} · adverb: {viably}
rely → adjective: {reliable} · noun: {reliability} · opposite adjective: {unreliable}
decide → noun: {decision} · adjective (firm, quick): {decisive} · opposite: {indecisive}
compete → noun (rivalry): {competition} · adjective: {competitive} · person: {competitor}
sustain → adjective: {sustainable} · noun: {sustainability} · opposite: {unsustainable}
predict → noun: {prediction} · adjective: {predictable} · opposite: {unpredictable}
strong → verb: {strengthen} · noun: {strength}
economy → adjective (of the economy): {economic} · adjective (saves money): {economical} · verb: {economise|economize}
deep → verb: {deepen} · noun: {depth}
persuade → noun: {persuasion} · adjective: {persuasive} · adverb: {persuasively}
account → adjective (responsible): {accountable} · noun: {accountability}
emphasis → verb: {emphasise|emphasize} · adjective: {emphatic}
